Piper Sandler kept its Overweight rating and $100 price target on AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS).

•	The firm said SpaceX’s push to compete for major U.S. carrier customers could encourage AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile to place greater value on ASTS’s direct-to-device broadband partnerships.

•	ASTS’s successful launch of BlueBird 11, 12, and 13 expands its constellation and supports its planned beta-service timeline.

•	Piper said the satellites reaching orbit increases its confidence in ASTS’s forecasts.

•	The target is based on 20x FY2031E EV/EBITDA, discounted at 15%, according to the note.

•	ASTS is scheduled to report earnings after the close on Monday, August 10.

US removes sanctions from IRGC-linked entities. U.S. Treasury removed counterterrorism sanctions from two aircraft and three airlines tied to Iran’s IRGC, according to OFAC’s website. Fly Baghdad Airlines and its fleet were delisted, but the airline’s CEO remains sanctioned.

What changed

•	Delisted: Fly Baghdad Airlines and its aircraft.

•	Still sanctioned: The CEO.

•	Original reason: The airline was sanctioned in January 2024 for allegedly helping the IRGC and proxy groups by moving fighters and weapons.

Why it matters

•	It signals a partial easing for some IRGC-linked aviation assets.

China expands countermeasures in U.S. trade fight

•	China barred domestic organizations and individuals from doing business with seven U.S. entities.

•	It tightened export controls on U.S.-bound drones and related tech.

•	It also restricted U.S. agencies’ role in mandatory Chinese factory certification inspections.

•	Beijing said the steps respond to recent U.S. restrictions on Chinese telecom, testing labs, drones, routers, submarine cables, robotics, and power inverters.

•	The move also follows Washington’s addition of 40+ Chinese entities to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act list.

What else changed

•	China placed Mesa, Arizona-based Compliance Testing LLC on its countermeasures list.

Japan weighs Palantir and Anduril AI for military overhaul — Nikkei Asia



Tokyo is reviewing U.S. AI platforms from Palantir and Anduril to modernize Japan’s military command-and-control ahead of a year-end security-document revision.

The Details:

•	Systems: Japan is considering Palantir’s Maven Smart System and Anduril’s Lattice AI.

•	Goal: The plan aims to speed combat decisions and align Japan with U.S. military operations.

•	Use cases: Officials are examining counterattacks, missile defense, and drone coordination.

•	Oversight: Japan is also weighing domestic data centers and a local AI layer for control.

Bottom Line: Japan is exploring U.S. battlefield AI, but wants domestic oversight for sensitive military data.
